patch.value: A colleague solves a linear system inside a hot loop with x = np.linalg.inv(A) @ b, where A is a 2000 x 2000 matrix and b is a vector. (a) What should they call instead, and why? Give two distinct reasons. (b) Their improved code raises numpy.linalg.LinAlgError: Singular matrix. What does this tell you about A and about how many solutions Ax = b can have?

A colleague solves a linear system inside a hot loop with x = np.linalg.inv(A) @ b. On every iteration both A (2000 x 2000) and the vector b are rebuilt from new data. (a) What should they call instead, and why? Give two distinct reasons. (b) Their improved code raises numpy.linalg.LinAlgError: Singular matrix. What does this tell you about A and about how many solutions Ax = b can have?
